title: Once-for-All subnetwork Mirror correction
hypothesis: Four per-subnetwork Givens angles over a frozen shared OFA-style slimmable MLP recover width/depth sharing interference on held-out digits at lower complete payload than independent subnetworks; equal-budget FiLM may explain the effect.
physical_object: one nested 64-wide two-hidden-layer MLP with shared ten-class output head
mirror_coordinate: four task-specific Givens angles applied to hidden coordinates 0-7 immediately before the shared classifier
logical_multiplicity: six subnets from widths [16,32,64] x depths [1,2]

data.split: stratified 60/20/20 train/validation/test, independently seeded by world

model.supernet_training: sandwich rule: largest and smallest subnet plus one sampled subnet each update; smaller logits distill from largest

controls: shared supernet plus four-angle Givens Mirror coordinate per subnet
shared supernet plus four-value grouped diagonal FiLM per subnet
shared supernet plus rank-1 output LoRA per subnet

development.selection_metric: mean validation NLL over all six architectures and methods
development.allowed_changes: select only the shared/independent training learning rate from the frozen two-value grid

storage.authority: actual torch.save inference bundle bytes plus canonical metadata, reloaded before evaluation
paid_objects: shared supernet or independent subnet weights

success_gate: For all three fresh worlds, Mirror mean accuracy improves >=1 percentage point over uncorrected shared supernet, stays within 2 points of independent subnetworks, and complete serialized bytes <=50% of independent. Mirror-specific: also beats FiLM by >=1 point at byte-near cost (within 15%) or saves >=10% bytes at <=0.5-point accuracy loss.
failure_gate: Miss shared/independent quality-storage gate in >=2 fresh worlds, or a simpler FiLM/LoRA control matches or dominates at equal/lower bytes and active compute.
boundaries: small OFA-style slimmable MLP, not published OFA reproduction
architecture count is not independent capacity
